subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw define first-class core/browser-plugin config and runtime APIs for per-profile browser proxies plus per-agent/subagent browser binding, or defer this to broader proxy/session design and external orchestration for now?
rationale: The requested feature adds public config and security-sensitive egress/session semantics across browser profiles, agents, and subagents, so automation cannot choose the product/security contract safely.

options.title: Design first-class browser contract
options.body: Specify and then implement the browser plugin/core contract for proxy secrets, SSRF policy, redaction, agent defaults, subagent inheritance, resource limits, and diagnostics before accepting code.

options.title: Split into narrower open issues
options.body: Use the open proxy issue and subagent browser ownership issue for their slices while keeping this umbrella open until both are resolved.

options.title: Defer to external orchestration
options.body: Document supported external approaches such as remote CDP, multiple gateways, or browser orchestration tools and avoid adding new core/browser config for now.

recommendation.title: Design first-class browser contract
recommendation.body: Specify and then implement the browser plugin/core contract for proxy secrets, SSRF policy, redaction, agent defaults, subagent inheritance, resource limits, and diagnostics before accepting code.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is ownership of the current browser plugin/runtime seam and adjacent subagent/thread design work.
